Tickets now on sale in local shops or via Even trite The new liturgical year starts next Sunday (First Sunday of Advent) when we enter Cycle Bof the Lectionary. For the most part in this new liturgical year, we will listen to the Gospel of St Mark. While Mark’s Gospel is presented in the Bible as the second of the four Gospels that we hear (Matthew, Mark, Luke & John), it is believed to have been the first written (probably be tween 50 – 70 AD), and directed to the needs of early Christian communities, particularly the Gent It is the shortest of the Gospels, with just 16 chapters. Jesus is pictured by Mark as a man of action and authority. He puts emphasis on what Jesus did, rather than on His words. Mark was not one of the apos tles chosen by Jesus, but he was a companion of Peter (Simon Peter) and much of what is written by Mar k draws from the preaching and eyewitness testimony of Peter, who had accompanied Jesus during His publ ic ministry. Most importantly, Mark’s Gospel gives us a clear p icture of what it means to be an authentic disciple or follower of Jesus. As disciples today, we are called to follow the example of Jesus. We pray that, in this coming liturgical year, as we listen to Gospel of St Mark, the Holy Spirit willg uide us in following Christ’s message in our daily lives, in all that we do and say.‘And at once they left their nets and followed him. ’ Mark 1:18St Mark, pray for us.
